comparison: Perfect alignment on molecular mechanism claims (C59-C67). Both evaluations find the IL-1β/IL1R1 and PSGL-1 signaling pathway evidence well-supported. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of experimental approaches while peer review acknowledges mechanisms were explored with well-designed experiments.

Complete agreement on human disease relevance (C9, C81-C87). Both accept the connection between defective neutrophil function and autoimmune liver disease in patient samples. OpenEval notes modest sample size and correlation vs causation uncertainty, while peer review fully accepts the association without reservations.

Significant disagreement on non-inflammatory nature (C10, C100-C102). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting evidence is observational rather than mechanistic and that 'immunologically silent' claim needs stronger support. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly affirming neutrophils clear cells 'without causing inflammation' as a key feature.

Strong alignment on autoantibody generation (C8, C77-C80). Both evaluations support the link between impaired clearance and autoimmunity. OpenEval notes mechanistic link requires further investigation, while peer review emphasizes this transforms understanding of neutrophil role in autoimmune disease pathogenesis.

Complete agreement on neutrophil depletion experiments (C6, C68-C76). Both find strong evidence that neutrophil depletion impairs apoptotic hepatocyte clearance and causes liver dysfunction. OpenEval highlights two independent depletion methods and statistical rigor, peer review explicitly affirms functional consequences.

Strong alignment on core discovery of neutrophil-mediated clearance (C3, C25-C27, C29-C32, C34-C35, C42-C44). Both evaluations strongly support this finding. Peer review also includes perforocytosis mechanism claims (C4-C5, C37-C48) in same result, calling it 'fundamental discovery.' OpenEval separates mechanism into distinct result R2.

Alignment on perforocytosis mechanism (C4-C5, C36-C48). OpenEval treats novel mechanism as separate supported finding with detailed assessment of imaging evidence. Peer review groups this with core neutrophil clearance discovery, with Reviewer 2 confirming visualization of perforocytosis and Reviewer 3 noting strong evidence for burrowing behavior.

Alignment on in vitro validation (C49-C54). OpenEval supports selectivity through negative controls and comparative assays. Peer review includes these claims in comprehensive affirmation of core findings, with all reviewers accepting experimental design quality.

Agreement on hepatocyte specificity (C55-C58). Both evaluations support selectivity data. OpenEval emphasizes flow cytometry and biochemical validation, peer review (Reviewer 3) explicitly acknowledges neutrophils remove apoptotic hepatocytes but not HEK293 or HUVEC cells.

Agreement on liver function consequences (C7, C75). Both support that impaired clearance affects liver function markers. OpenEval treats as separate result with standard markers, peer review integrates into broader depletion findings statement.

Alignment on synthesis and significance (C88, C106). Both accept homeostatic role and broader implications. OpenEval supports based on collective evidence integration, peer review calls it 'fundamental discovery' that 'transforms' understanding of neutrophil biology.

Agreement on neutrophil abundance rationale (C92, C108). Both accept that neutrophil abundance supports their role in routine clearance. OpenEval bases on established knowledge, peer review acknowledges neutrophils as most abundant circulating leukocytes.

Agreement on compensatory macrophage response (C93-C94). Both support evidence of macrophage compensation after neutrophil depletion. OpenEval notes system-level compensation with some uncertainty about efficiency, peer review implicitly accepts as part of depletion study results.

Agreement on cell-type specificity (C95-C96). Both support selectivity for hepatocytes. OpenEval emphasizes negative controls and reasonable speculation about distinct signals, peer review acknowledges specificity data without challenge.

Disagreement on causality in disease (C11, C104). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mouse model shows sufficiency not necessity and human data are correlative. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the causal connection and transformative implications for understanding autoimmune disease pathogenesis.

Partial overlap on disease causation (C11). OpenEval expresses uncertainty about directionality and causality in human disease, requiring additional evidence. Peer review accepts broader significance for understanding neutrophil role in disease without questioning causality.

Agreement on speculative nature of therapeutic implications (C115). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable hypothesis lacking experimental support. Peer review accepts within broader significance statement but does not specifically validate therapeutic claims.

Agreement that functional benefit speculation (C109) lacks direct testing. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN for bile acid leakage prevention hypothesis. Peer review implicitly accepts within compensatory mechanism discussion but does not specifically validate this speculation.

OpenEval separately evaluates background/context claims (C1-C2, C12-C24, C33, C89-C91, C97-C99, C103, C105, C107, C110-C114) as supported established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer review does not separately assess background claims.
OpenEval supports inference about rarity of apoptotic hepatocytes (C28) as consistent with efficient clearance. Peer review does not separately evaluate this contextual claim.

OpenEval identifies speculative claims (C40, C109, C115) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are reasonable hypotheses lacking experimental support. Peer review does not separately flag these as speculative, incorporating them into broader acceptance of findings and significance.
